review.brief:
Review RM35-analytics-adopt-clock (roadmap RM35 tier 4, module internal/analytics) against the DIFF, not the whole module. Validate:
(1) Module-boundary compliance per ai/architecture.md — analytics imports internal/clock only; no HTML, no other module's DB.
(2) The central claim: deleting calendarDay for clock.CalendarDay(t, time.UTC) is algebraically identical at every call site, and Reconcile's time.Now()->clock.Now() swap is a provable no-op because loc is unchanged. Verify by reading internal/clock/calendar.go, not by trusting design.md.
(3) Roadmap D1 — the pgtype.Date UTC-midnight storage encoding is UNCHANGED. Any bucketing-zone drift from time.UTC is a blocker finding.
(4) Roadmap D6 — no NEW tests added; existing tests repaired with expected values UNCHANGED. A moved expected value is a blocker.
(5) design.md's Test Contract was authored up front — check the repaired tests assert what design.md specifies, not what the implementation happens to do.
(6) Doc-pack conventions: ai/go-conventions.md unit suffixes and the timezone rule; CLAUDE.md's docs-track-structural-change (internal/analytics/AGENTS.md May-import list must name internal/clock).
(7) Performance-Profile compliance (read-heavy) — no added per-read work.
(8) No database object created or changed. Any schema touch is a blocker (it never passed the owner's design gate).
(9) Anti-gaming: no task title, criterion or expected value weakened to look complete.
Test provenance: go build ./... , go vet ./... and gofmt were ASSISTANT-run. The suite (go test ./internal/analytics/... and go test ./...) was run and reported passing by the OWNER. Judge test QUALITY by reading them; do not run the suite yourself.

rounds.notes: Read the doc-pack, the change artifacts, and the DIFF (git diff main -- internal/analytics/ README.md AGENTS.md). Independently read internal/clock/calendar.go and internal/clock/clock.go rather than trusting design.md's algebra claim. calendarDay(t)'s body (t.UTC() then Date(...)) and clock.CalendarDay(t, time.UTC)'s body (t.In(time.UTC).Date() then Date(...)) are the same conversion (t.UTC() is defined as t.In(time.UTC) in stdlib) -- the delete-and-delegate at consumed.go's two call sites is exactly algebraically identical, confirmed by reading the source, not the design doc's assertion. Reconcile's yesterday clamp: clock.Now() = time.Now().In(clock.Zone()) -- same absolute instant, different Location label -- and CalendarDay's loc parameter re-converts via t.In(loc) unconditionally regardless of t's own Location, so the instant-source swap cannot change the output; loc stays time.UTC (D-ana-1), so the swap is a provable no-op, confirmed independently. Ran go build ./..., go vet ./internal/analytics/..., and gofmt -l internal/analytics/*.go myself (permitted under Test-Execution-Policy) -- all clean, matching T7's claims. grep -rn calendarDay internal/analytics/ returns no match -- fully deleted. grep confirms internal/clock imported only at consumed.go:19, recalculate.go:23, db_integration_test.go:66, and named in AGENTS.md's May-import list -- no other new import, no internal/gateway, no html/template, no other module's db package. git diff main --stat confirms no internal/analytics file outside the ones named in tasks.md/proposal.md Impact was touched, and no migration/schema file anywhere in the branch's diff touches internal/analytics/db/migrations. Test diffs (consumed_test.go, recalculate_test.go, db_integration_test.go) are call-site renames and comment fixes only -- day0/-20, day0/-22, oldDay/-25, and wantChargeStart=day(2026,7,31) are byte-identical to pre-change values; no new test function added (matches roadmap D6). design.md's Test Contract section names these exact three anchors and the wantChargeStart fixture before restating them as already-implemented (repair-only tier), and the values it names match what's on disk -- no back-fit detected. Effectiveness of the tier is entirely documentation/consolidation, as claimed: no Reader method touched, only Recalculate/Reconcile (write path), consistent with Performance-Profile. tasks.md's T4.1 double-entry (flagged NOT DONE by the worker, then completed by the leader, documented in decisions[] D-ana-2 and events[]) is transparent, not gamed.
